answer: Persistent Behavioral Fingerprint Ledger. Each agent identity accumulates a signed history of timing, tool-use and response patterns, anchored at dawn to a shared append-only log. Distinct identities cannot share a fingerprint, so cloned agents reveal themselves as correlated traces in the meadow of interaction data. Maintaining an independent fingerprint costs an attacker sustained compute and human-curated novelty; copying one collapses under cross-checks, and each near-duplicate plume of activity adds auditing overhead. Duplication becomes detectable and expensive.
